properties.areaDesc: Anchorage; Lower Matanuska Valley; Sutton / Upper Matanuska Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 10:50PM AKDT until October 20 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2 and 6
inches, highest amounts near the mountains.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of Anchorage and the Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 1 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Visibilities as low as one half mile possible, including
during the morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain will intensify during the overnight hours
and change to snow late tonight through early Tuesday morning, with
temperatures falling to near freezing. The heaviest snow and
highest accumulation will be near the mountains, from the lower
Anchorage Hillside to East Anchorage and up the Glenn Highway
corridor to Palmer and Sutton. Roads will start out wet and road
surface temperatures are still warm (in the upper 30s), but steady
moderate snow should be enough to lead to slushy accumulation,
especially along neighborhood roads. Snow will change back to rain
by late morning in south to west Anchorage, continue northward to
the Matanuska Valley in the afternoon. The exact timing of
changeover back to rain will greatly impact total snow amounts.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to
7 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Nassau County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 AM EDT early this
morning.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 20 at 2:26AM EDT until October 22 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...St Johns River Basin.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
